description: Interactive browser workbench, Python library, and CLI that classifies canonical-versus-isoform protein deletion topology via affine-gap BLOSUM62 alignment and profiles multimer interface conservation, destabilization, ablation, and emergence across ipTM, ipSAE_min, and 3D dimer coordinates.

function.note: Derives splice isoform deletion intervals and classifies multimer interface state transitions.

name: isoform-grammar

metadata.abstract: Alternative splicing and proteolytic truncation generate tens of thousands of protein isoforms in the human proteome. Their consequences for quaternary state, the level at which most protein function operates, have been examined largely one molecule at a time. Using the AlphaFold Protein Structure Database expansion to predicted human homodimers, we compared 5,168 canonical-versus-truncated pairs on four interface metrics distributed with that release. Truncation partitions high-confidence canonical homodimers into structural conservation (56.4% of pairs), complete interface ablation (26.1%) and partial destabilization (17.5%). The partition holds on predicted interface size and not only on interface confidence. Conservation events retain a median 0.938 of the canonical interface residues, destabilization events 0.622, and ablation events 0.000. Interface loss is graded by deletion magnitude, falling from 0.997 of the interface retained below a tenth of the chain removed to 0.192 above a half (Spearman rho = -0.552, p = 4.5 × 10  −61 ). Deletion topology, derived by global alignment, is 53.3% N-terminal and 42.7% C-terminal. C-terminal truncation lowers interface conservation from 65.4% to 37.5%, an asymmetry confined to deletions above the cohort median of 89 residues. Of 208 pairs in which ipTM reports emergence from a sub-threshold canonical baseline, 42 reproduce on ipSAE, the metric on which the release defines its tiers. Canonical disorder content shows no detectable difference between emergence events and controls matched on canonical confidence. Predicted confidence tracks deposited structures, with two or more copies in a deposited assembly for 95.3% of high-confidence canonicals against 49.9% of low-confidence canonicals. Emergence-cohort canonicals are enriched for established homomers, 75.0% against 48.7% for other canonicals of the same confidence, so emergence marks full-length predictions that fail and not interfaces created by truncation. Truncation-associated remodeling of homodimer architecture is a graded, topology-asymmetric property of the human proteome, readable from interface size and operating across gene-functional categories.
metadata.title: Structural grammar of truncation across the human homodimer landscape
